problem: The text says the friction estimate uses b ≈ 1.5, which with σ̄ = 350 MPa gives p = 525 ln R, but the plotted friction curve is 520 ln R (b ≈ 1.49). A student comparing text and figure sees two slightly different constants.
fix: Make the figure match the text: use p = 525 ln R and say it is 1.5 times the ideal curve, or state in the text 'b ≈ 1.49, about 1.5' and keep 520 ln R.

problem: 'about 1.49 times higher at every R' can be misread as 149 % higher; the ratio of the two curves is 1.49, so the pressure is 49 % higher.
fix: Say 'the friction curve is 1.49 times the ideal pressure, that is 49 % higher at every R'.

problem: F = σ̄wL and T = FL/2 are the simplest estimates. They leave out the friction-hill multiplier on roll pressure (typically about 1.1–1.2 in hot rolling) and the mill/transmission efficiency, so the computed force and power are lower bounds presented as exact.
fix: Add one line: real mills multiply F by a friction-hill factor near 1.1–1.2 and need motor power P = 2Tω/η with η the drive efficiency, typically 0.8–0.9.

problem: P = 2Tω assumes both rolls are driven. If only one roll is driven the motor supplies Tω, not 2Tω. The chapter does not state this assumption, though the 'factor 2' trap depends on it.
fix: Write: 'P = 2Tω when both rolls are driven (the usual case); with one driven roll P = Tω.'

problem: 'Extrusion force is p times ram area' leaves the ram area unnamed. The ram area is the billet cross-section A₀, not the product area A_f used in R, and students mix the two.
fix: Write: 'Extrusion force F = p A₀, where A₀ is the billet (container) cross-section, the area the ram pushes on.'
